correctness.rationale: Kaib--Werner Proposition 6.12(2) makes every multiplication map finite, flat and surjective, hence N[m] is finite flat of generic rank m^(2g-t_eta). The special identity component has m-torsion length m^(2g-t_s). Over the algebraically closed residue field, every m-torsion component has an m-torsion representative and each intersection is a translate of the identity-component kernel, giving |Phi_s[m]|=m^(t_s-t_eta). Lemma 5.11 makes Phi_s divisible, and the classification of divisible abelian groups then gives torsion (Q/Z)^(t_s-t_eta). The proof uses lengths, not reduced point counts, so it also covers residue characteristic dividing m.

evidence: Conrad's semistable-reduction notes summarize Grothendieck's theorem: in the rank-one abelian setting, the direct limit over ramified extensions is Hom(X(T),Q/Z).

value.rationale: The result is a structural refinement of the new higher-rank Néron theory: it turns qualitative divisibility into an exact degeneration invariant and identifies each unit of torus-rank jump with one Q/Z torsion direction in the actual component group. Component groups and torus ranks are basic reduction invariants, and the formula works simultaneously at every point of an arbitrary-rank valuation spectrum, giving a quantitative analogue of a classical rank-one direct-limit phenomenon.
